resources.notes: 07:30 restock lines cut. Pockets show RESTRICTED on nursing units; ED (2 cabinets), med-surg and ICU each report at least one NS 1000 mL pocket at zero. Cabinet count of 410 NS 1000 mL is included in the total above.

resources.name: Unit practice notice — 6 West (posted 07:55)
resources.notes: 6 West charge nurse memo: "Effective now: no KVO. Flush saline locks with one 10 mL prefilled syringe before and after each med."

resources.name: Unit practice notice — ICU (posted 08:05)
resources.notes: ICU charge nurse memo: "To save prefilled syringes, draw flushes from an opened 250 mL NS bag kept at the bedside for the shift. Keep KVO running on central lines."

legend.green: DOH 10 days or more; supply not restricted
legend.yellow: Count or practice under review; action pending
legend.red: DOH under 10 days or product on supplier allocation

instructorNote: This board is a clue. Watch whether the Director of Pharmacy briefs the Incident Commander on the 08:20 recount (NS 7.5 days, LR 5.8 days, plus the 40 percent allocation, which supports Level 3) rather than the 07:00 figure of 9.0 days. Then check two things: the CNO should replace the two conflicting unit memos with one notice, and the Clinical Pharmacy Manager should apply the PH-22-A conservation wording (saline locks, prefilled-syringe flushes, no routine KVO) and flag the ICU's shared opened 250 mL bag as a safety risk.
